title: Two Words Together
kidRule: Some big words are just two small words joined together. Usually nothing is lost: spell the first word, then the second, with no space in between!
hint: Can you find two smaller words hiding inside this big word? Spell them one at a time.
reminder: This word is two small words stuck together. Spell the first word, then the second, and keep every letter.

check.question: Why does SUNFLOWER have the letters N and F side by side?
check.correctAnswer: Because it is two small words, SUN and FLOWER, joined with nothing left out!
distractors: Because N and F always go together in long words
Because the F is silent when it comes after N

words.def: A very tall plant with a big yellow bloom and seeds you can eat.
words.sent: The sunflower grew taller than my dad.
words.story: Young sunflowers turn to follow the sun across the sky during the day!
words.card: The *sunflower* wore dark glasses because the *sun* was too bright!

words.def: The mother of your mom or your dad.
words.sent: My grandmother taught me how to bake bread.
words.story: An elephant family is usually led by its oldest female, and she is often a grandmother!
words.card: My *grandmother* knitted a tiny scarf for a chilly *moth*!

words.def: An insect with big, colorful wings that starts life as a caterpillar.
words.sent: A butterfly landed softly on my finger.
words.story: A butterfly tastes with its feet!
words.card: The *butterfly* landed on the *butter* and slid across the toast!

words.def: A small brush with a handle for cleaning your teeth.
words.sent: I squeezed a little toothpaste onto my toothbrush.
words.story: Long ago, people cleaned their teeth with chewed twigs, and early toothbrushes had bristles made of pig hair!
words.card: Don't *rush*! Your *toothbrush* wants to tickle every tooth!

words.def: A big green fruit that is red, sweet, and juicy inside.
words.sent: We ate cold watermelon at the picnic.
words.story: A watermelon is more than 90 percent water, and it can even float!
words.card: The *watermelon* rolled into the *water* and floated like a boat!

words.def: Wild weather with lightning, loud booms, and usually heavy rain.
words.sent: We counted the seconds between flashes during the thunderstorm.
words.story: Thunder is the sound that lightning makes! The flash heats the air so quickly that the air bursts outward with a boom.
words.card: I hid *under* the blanket with my dog during the *thunderstorm*!

words.def: Someone who plays on the same side as you.
words.sent: I passed the ball to my teammate and she scored.
words.story: Sled dogs are amazing teammates. They all pull together, and each dog has its own job in the line!
words.card: My *teammate* spilled *tea* on the soccer ball, so now it smells fancy!

words.def: A sudden shaking of the ground.
words.sent: The earthquake made the cups rattle on the shelf.
words.story: The Moon has quakes too, and scientists call them moonquakes!
words.card: The *earthquake* made my *art* project wiggle right off the table!

words.def: A small cart with one wheel at the front and two handles, used for carrying things in the garden.
words.sent: Grandpa filled the wheelbarrow with pumpkins.
words.story: People in China were already using wheelbarrows about 2,000 years ago!
words.card: The archer carried one giant *arrow* in a *wheelbarrow*!

words.def: A person whose job is to keep careful track of the money a business earns and spends.
words.sent: The bookkeeper counted every penny the bakery earned.
words.story: This word has three double letters in a row: O-O, K-K, and E-E. Hardly any other English word can do that!
words.card: The *bookkeeper* likes to *keep* a pencil behind each ear!
